title: Two-on-One Transition Push
description: Two attackers push a fast break the length of the court against one retreating defender, reading the defender's chair position to decide between a pass and a direct finish.

content.objective: Push the break under control and read the single defender to choose between a pass and a direct finish.
content.setup: Two attackers start under one basket with a ball; one defender starts near the far free-throw line.
instructions: Both attackers push hard down the floor, staying wide to keep the defender from covering both.
The ball handler reads which attacker the defender commits to.
Pass to the open attacker, or push directly to the rim if the defender commits to the pass.
Finish under control; do not force a contested shot if the pass was clearly open.
coachingPoints: Keep real width between the two attackers so the defender genuinely can't cover both.
Make the read early, well before reaching the defender.
Push with full strokes even at speed — a rushed, choppy push loses control of the chair.
commonMistakes: Both attackers pushing the same lane, erasing the numbers advantage.
Forcing a pass when the lane to the rim was actually open.
Forcing a play before the numbers advantage is actually clear.
content.safety: Make sure the full-court lane is clear of other groups before pushing at speed.
progressions: Add a second trailing defender for a three-on-two version once decisions are consistently good.
regressions: Walk through the spacing and the read once at a slow push before running it live.
